title: EU leaders agree 90 billion euro loan for Ukraine without using frozen Russian assets
body:
On 19 December 2025, European Union leaders meeting at a summit in Brussels agreed a 90 billion euro loan to cover Ukraine's looming budget shortfalls. The loan runs for two years and is backed by the EU's common budget. Ursula von der Leyen said Ukraine would repay it only once Moscow paid for the damage it had caused.

A plan to use about 200 billion euros of frozen Russian central bank assets was dropped. Belgium, where most of the assets are held, demanded guarantees on sharing liability, and other countries would not accept them. Joint debt requires unanimity among the EU's 27 members, so Hungary, Slovakia and Czechia were exempted from the commitment in order to avoid blocking the deal. The EU estimated that Ukraine needed an extra 135 billion euros over the next two years, and the cash shortage was expected to begin in April.

Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever said "rationality has prevailed." German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, who had pushed for the asset plan, said the loan sent a clear signal to Vladimir Putin. President Volodymyr Zelensky called it significant support, stressed that Russian assets must remain immobilised, and said Ukraine needed a financial security guarantee. Kremlin negotiator Kirill Dmitriev welcomed the failure to use the assets. French President Emmanuel Macron said Europe should find a way to re-engage Moscow in coming weeks. US President Donald Trump kept pressing for a quick deal to end the war.
